They're trying to hail us now.|Carklin Ryoon, upon seeing three ''Imperial II''-class Star Destroyers emerge from hyperspace|audio=Ryoon.flac|}} The '''''Imperial II''-class Star Destroyer''', also known as the '''Class II Star Destroyer''' and as the '''Impstar-Deuce''' by the rebels, was a [[Star Destroyer]] model manufactured by [[Kuat Drive Yards]] for use by the [[Imperial Navy]]. Part of the [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer|''Imperial''-class line]], the class served as successor to the [[Imperial I-class Star Destroyer|''Imperial I''-class Star Destroyer]]. Armed with a plethora of weapons, including [[turbolaser]]s and [[ion cannon]]s, the 1,600-[[meter]]-long [[capital ship]] could be used to [[Space warfare|subjugate]] a [[planet]] or serve as a [[command ship]] for other [[Starship|vessels]]. Following the [[death]] of [[Galactic Emperor|Emperor]] [[Darth Sidious|Palpatine]] in [[4 ABY]], the ''Imperial II''-class Star Destroyer ''[[Torment]]'' was dispatched to [[Naboo]] as part of [[Operation: Cinder]], an order from the late Emperor to destroy Imperial planets with [[Climate disruption array|satellites]]. However, the [[Battle of Theed|attack]] was thwarted by the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebel Alliance]] and the ''Torment'' was destroyed before it could withdraw. Later in the [[Contingency]], in [[5 ABY]], many Imperial IIs took part in the [[Battle of Jakku]] against the [[New Republic]], although the Star Destroyers fled from the battle. They were later [[Destruction of Imperial Star Destroyers|destroyed]] by the [[Sovereign Latitudes of Maracavanya]]'s [[Executor-class Star Dreadnought|''Executor''-class Star Dreadnought]] ''[[Liberty's Misrule]]''. ==Characteristics== ===General characteristics=== [[File:Torment-ShatteredEmpire3.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The ''Torment'' was an ''Imperial II''-class Star Destroyer.]] Part of the [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer|''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer]] line, the ''Imperial II''-class [[Star Destroyer]] was a [[capital ship]] model built by [[Kuat Drive Yards]] for the [[Imperial Navy]] to replace the [[Imperial I-class Star Destroyer|''Imperial I''-class Star Destroyer]]. Like its predecessor, the ''Imperial II''-class measured 1,600 [[meter]]s in length, was painted a light shade of [[Color|gray]], was wedge-shaped and had a raised [[Conning tower|bridge tower]]. It was outwardly nearly indistinguishable to its predecessor but possessed several key differences such as a [[communications tower]] between its two [[deflector shield generator dome]]s instead of a [[tractor beam targeting array]], heavier armament, a reinforced hull, and more advanced deflector shields. ''Imperial II''-class Star Destroyers were powered by a [[solar ionization reactor]] located on the ventral [[hull]].[[Shattered Empire 2|''Shattered Empire'' 2]] Internal defenses were installed within the ship, consisting of [[Stormtrooper armor|stormtrooper helmet]]-sized exhaust ports built into at least one spacious room that emitted [[fire]] capable of incapacitating [[armor]]ed [[Trooper|troops]]. At least one [[airlock]] was located near the meridian trenches at the side of the Star Destroyer, and the vessel also contained at least one [[Garbage compactor|trash compactor]] connected with passageways large enough to transport stormtroopers into the waste facility. The Star Destroyer also contained a briefing room where new assignments and mission briefings could be given, with two [["Tulip" style Imperial work station]]s located within.''[[Star Wars: Squadrons]]'' ===Propulsion=== Ships of the class were propelled by three KDY [[Destroyer-I ion engine]]s, and they also had four backup [[Cygnus Spaceworks]] [[Gemon-4 ion engine]]s. This allowed for speeds of 60 [[Megalight per hour|MGLT]] in [[realspace]] and 975 [[Kilometer per hour|kilometers per hour]] in an [[atmosphere]]. A [[hyperdrive]] was also equipped, allowing the ships to travel in [[hyperspace]]. Before the ship could jump, all stations initiated a pre-jump procedure during which the engines powered up, the [[hangar]] bays were cleared of non-Imperial starships and the trash was gathered in the [[Garbage compactor|trash disposal]] section to be ejected. This lengthy process took more than 40 [[Standard minute|minutes]], after which the ship jumped to hyperspace.{{StoryCite|story=Standard Imperial Procedure|book=From a Certain Point of View: The Empire Strikes Back}} ===Weapons systems and complement=== {{Quote|The Impstar-Deuce has a complement of seventy-two TIE fighters, princess.|Shara Bey, to Leia Organa, upon their approach to the ''Torment''|}} Like all ''Imperial''-class vessels, ''Imperial II''-class Star Destroyers were armed with sixty [[turbolaser]] batteries, sixty heavy [[ion cannon]] emplacements, and ten [[tractor beam projector]]s. The ships [[Carrier|carried]] with them seventy-two [[TIE series|TIE fighter series]] starfighters, eight [[Lambda-class T-4a shuttle|''Lambda''-class T-4a shuttles]], twenty [[All Terrain Armored Transport (Galactic Civil War)|All Terrain Armored Transports]] and thirty [[All Terrain Scout Transport]]s, the latter two of which were transported to [[planet]]ary surfaces by at least two [[Gozanti-class cruiser|''Gozanti''-class cruisers]]. All these vessels were stored in the ships' two large hangar bays, which were located side by side in the anterior wall of an indentation in the ventral hull. 9,700 [[stormtrooper]]s crewed the Star Destroyer, along with various other [[Imperial Military]] personnel such as [[Imperial Starfighter Pilot|TIE fighter pilots]] and [[Imperial officer]]s. [[MSE-6 series repair droid]]s were also present in the ship's corridors. Two [[Standard year|years]] worth of consumables were kept on the vessels to maintain the crew. ===Bridge=== {{Quote|Clear the bridge!|Captain Lerr Duvat, upon the arrival of the Emperor's messenger|}} [[File:TormentsBridge-ShatteredEmpire2.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The bridge of the ''Imperial II''-class Star Destroyer ''Torment''.]] Organized almost identically to that of the ''Imperial I''-class,''[[Star Wars Rebels: Spark of Rebellion]]'' the ''Imperial II''-class had a command [[Bridge (starship)|bridge]] with a central command walkway and two [[data pit]]s[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2016)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']] where [[Galactic Empire|Imperial]] [[officer]]s operated their console stations, which were arranged perpendicular to the central walkway. The pits acted as a separator between the bridge technicians and their higher-ups, giving an illustration of the chain of command within the ship. These pits had an entrance each in the same direction as with the upper doorway. The [[human]]-sized frames led to corridors of the same level, through which a [[scomp link]] socket that interacted with the starship's computer systems responsible for internal defense, airlock-, and waste collection-management was installed at an [[astromech droid]]-height. ==Role== An ''Imperial II''-class Star Destroyer was capable of [[Command ship|commanding]] an [[Space warfare|assault]] on an entire planet, which could include controlling smaller siege vessels or using its large carrying capacity to deliver a surface assault force. The ship could also form part of a [[fleet]].''[[Dawn of Rebellion]]'' ==History== ===Early history=== By [[9 BBY]],"[[Part V]]" features the ''[[Devastator]]''{{'s}} first chronological appearance. {{KenobiDate|V}} As such, the ''Devastator'' must have been commissioned in or before that year. Kuat Drive Yards had stopped manufacturing the ''Imperial I''-class with the production of the ''[[Devastator]]'', the final ship of its class. Some Imperial Is, including the ''Devastator'', were upgraded to feature bridges with communication towers,The ''[[Devastator]]'', identified as an [[Imperial I-class Star Destroyer|''Imperial I''-class Star Destroyer]] in ''[[Ultimate Star Wars]]'', is shown in [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']] featuring what the [[Droids in Distress (book)|''Droids in Distress'' book]] identifies as a [[tractor beam targeting array]]. In the short story "[[Blade Squadron (short story)|Blade Squadron]]," the ''Devastator'' is shown at the [[Battle of Endor]] with what {{SWCT|set=Blueprints|cardname=Star Destroyer}} shows to be a [[communications tower]]. As ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' places the events of ''A New Hope'' prior to the Battle of Endor, the ''Devastator'' must have had its tractor beam targeting array replaced with a communications tower. like Imperial IIs. Around [[5 BBY]], Kuat Drive Yards began production of the ''Imperial II''-class. In or before [[1 BBY]],''Imperial II''-class [[Star Destroyer]]s were stationed at [[Scarif]] when the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|Death Star]] was operational, according to ''[[Dawn of Rebellion]]''. As the [[Space station|station]] was [[Battle of Yavin|destroyed]] in [[1 BBY]] per ''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'', the ''Imperial II''-classes must have been stationed at Scarif in or before that [[Standard year|year]]. at least four ''Imperial II''-class Star Destroyers were amongst roughly twenty ships in an Imperial Navy fleet above the planet [[Scarif]], home of the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|Death Star]] [[battle station]]. ===The ''Torment''{{'s}} attack=== {{Quote|I've got an ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer at two-two mark six…''"
"''…Looks like a Deuce.''"
"''Well, we knew this wouldn't be easy…|Shara Bey, Leia Organa and Sosha Soruna discuss the ''Torment''|}} Seventeen [[Standard day|days]] after the [[Battle of Endor]] in [[4 ABY]],''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' which had seen the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebel Alliance]] defeat the Galactic Empire with the [[death]] of Emperor Palpatine,{{Film|VI}} and subsequent retreat of remaining Imperial forces, the ''Imperial II''-class Star Destroyer ''[[Torment]]'' was visited by a [[Sentinel (Contingency)|messenger]] [[droid]]. The droid delivered a posthumous message from the Emperor, ordering the ship's [[captain]], [[Lerr Duvat]], to scour the planet [[Naboo]] using [[Climate disruption array|weather-altering satellites]], as part of the [[Contingency]]'s [[Operation: Cinder]], an Imperial plan to ensure both the Empire and its enemies would fall following the Emperor's death. [[File:RestorationVsTorment-ShatteredEmpire3.png|thumb|left|300px|The ''Torment'' was destroyed by the ''Restoration''.]] Assisted by [[Lieutenant]] [[Gulin]], Duvat immediately set course for Naboo. Upon the ''Torment''{{'s}} arrival at the planet, he deployed the [[satellite]]s in order to create massive storms across Naboo. However, a [[Flight group|group]] of [[N-1 starfighter]]s from Naboo, [[pilot]]ed by the rebels [[Shara Bey]], [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]] and [[Sosha Soruna]], [[Battle of Theed|attacked]] the satellites. In retaliation, the Star Destroyer's complement of TIE fighters was deployed to engage the attackers. Just as the three [[starfighter]]s were about to be destroyed by the TIEs, the Rebel Alliance arrived with the [[MC80 Star Cruiser]] ''[[Restoration]]'' and many starfighters including [[Danger Squadron]], a [[squadron]] of [[T-65B X-wing starfighter|X-wing starfighters]] led by Rebel veteran Shriv Suurgav and Imperial defectors Iden Versio and Del Meeko of Inferno Squad. Together with the Naboo starfighters, they destroyed the remainder of the satellites and the ''Torment'', despite an attempt by the Star Destroyer to withdraw. Before its destruction, however, the ''Torment'' managed to deploy part of its planetary assault force, which briefly attacked Naboo's [[capital]] of [[Theed]] before being neutralized by an ion pulse from the [[Theed Royal Palace]], and then captured. ===Project Starhawk=== In 4 ABY,''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the main events of ''[[Star Wars: Squadrons]]'' to [[4 ABY]]. during the [[Battle of Yavin Prime]], the [[New Republic]], the Rebel Alliance's successor state, had successfully captured the ''Imperial II''-class Star Destroyer ''[[Victorum]]'' for usage in [[Project Starhawk]]. After they [[Defense of the Victorum|defended]] the ''Victorum'' from Imperial forces, it arrived at the [[Nadiri Dockyards]], where it and other Imperial vessels were salvaged for the new prototype of the [[Starhawk-class battleship|''Starhawk''-class battleship]], the ''[[Starhawk]]''.''[[Star Wars: Squadrons]]'' ===Eleodie Maracavanya's find=== {{Quote|These ships are running. Look at the battle damage—they've taken fire, and recently. And behold those hyperspeed vectors—they're coming from near to the Unknown. They're coming from ''Jakku''. We do a little cleanup here for the New Republic, then we send them the bill.|Eleodie Maracavanya explains the plan to destroy the three ''Imperial II''-class Star Destroyers to the ''Liberty's Misrule''{{'s}} crew|audio=Marcavanya-ImpII.flac|}} In [[5 ABY]],''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' cites the [[Battle of Jakku]] as taking place in [[5 ABY]]. As the ''Imperial II''-class' [[Destruction of Imperial Star Destroyers|appearance]] in ''[[Aftermath: Empire's End]]'' takes place concurrently to the battle, the event in question must also take place in that [[Standard year|year]]. three ''Imperial II''-class Star Destroyers were part of the Imperial Navy, which fought in the [[Battle of Jakku]] against the New Republic. However, the Star Destroyers fled from [[Jakku]], and after jumping out of hyperspeed in [[Wild Space]], their captains attempted to seek solace with a small fleet of ships led by the [[Executor-class Star Dreadnought|''Executor''-class Star Dreadnought]]''[[Star Wars: The Rebel Files]]'' ''[[Liberty's Misrule]]'', which they thought was another Imperial remnant. However, the fleet was actually under the command of [[pirate]] [[Eleodie Maracavanya]] of the [[Sovereign Latitudes of Maracavanya]]. Maracavanya deduced that the ships had come from Jakku, and ordered the [[Destruction of Imperial Star Destroyers|destruction]] of the vessels, much to the surprise of crew member [[Carklin Ryoon]]. Maracavanya then elaborated on the decision to the ''Liberty's Misrule''{{'s}} crew, citing that the New Republic could grant the group some legitimacy if they destroyed the vessels, as it was likely they would appreciate the cleanup following their battle. All vessels then opened fire on the three Star Destroyers, with Maracavanya believing they stood no chance of survival. ==Behind the scenes== ===Notable appearances=== The ''Imperial II''-class Star Destroyer debuted in the ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]] in [[Shattered Empire 2|''Shattered Empire'' 2]], a [[2015]] [[Star Wars comic books|comic]] written by [[Greg Rucka]] and illustrated by [[Marco Checchetto]], [[Emilio Laiso]] and [[Angel Unzueta]]. Although the ''Torment''{{'s}} class was not mentioned in the issue, it would later be identified as an Impstar-Deuce in the next issue of the [[Star Wars: Shattered Empire|series]], [[Shattered Empire 3|''Shattered Empire'' 3]], which was also written by Rucka. The class' full name was revealed in the [[2016]] reference book ''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: The Ultimate Visual Guide]]'', written by [[Pablo Hidalgo]]. The [[Imperial II-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial II''-class Star Destroyer]] was originally created for''[[Star Wars: X-Wing Alliance]]'', a [[Star Wars Legends|Legends]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]], confirms that the [[Avenger/Legends|''Avenger'']], featured in the film [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']] and its [[Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back (novelization)|novelization]], was an [[Imperial II-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial II''-class Star Destroyer]]. Therefore, that class of [[Starship/Legends|ship]] appeared in those stories. the [[1980]] film [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']]. In ''Legends'', the ''Imperial II''-class [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]] first appeared in the [[Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back (novelization)|''The Empire Strikes Back''{{'s}} novelization]], written by [[Donald F. Glut]], which was released in the same year as the film itself.[[Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode V: The Empire Strikes Back'' novelization]] However, the ship's class was not revealed until the term ISD II was used by the [[1989]] supplement ''[[The Star Wars Rules Companion]]'',''[[The Star Wars Rules Companion]]'' and the term Imperial II Star Destroyer was used by the ''[[Imperial Sourcebook]]'', also released in 1989.''[[Imperial Sourcebook]]'' ===Inconsistencies=== [[File:Torment-ShatteredEmpire2.png|thumb|right|250px|The incorrect depiction of the ''Torment'']] On the first page of ''Shattered Empire, Part II'', illustrated by Emilio Laiso, the ''Torment'' was mistakenly depicted with the targeting array of an ''Imperial I''-class Star Destroyer.[[Droids in Distress (book)|''Droids in Distress'' chapter book]] This was rectified in the last page of the same issue, this time drawn by Marco Checchetto, as well as in its later appearances in ''Shattered Empire, Part III'' and ''[[Star Wars Battlefront II]]''. ==Appearances== {{ScrollBox|content= *''[[Star Wars: Battlefront II]]'' *[[Star Wars (2015) 35|''Star Wars'' (2015) 35]] *[[Star Wars (2015) 36|''Star Wars'' (2015) 36]] *{{StoryCite|story=R2-D2 and the Renegade Rescue|book=Galactic Adventures Storybook Collection|audiobook=2}} *[[Doctor Aphra (2016) 20|''Doctor Aphra'' (2016) 20]] *[[Star Wars (2015) 48|''Star Wars'' (2015) 48]] *[[Star Wars (2015) 49|''Star Wars'' (2015) 49]] *[[Star Wars (2015) 52|''Star Wars'' (2015) 52]] *[[Star Wars (2015) 53|''Star Wars'' (2015) 53]] *[[Star Wars (2015) 54|''Star Wars'' (2015) 54]] *[[Star Wars (2015) 55|''Star Wars'' (2015) 55]] *[[Star Wars (2015) 73|''Star Wars'' (2015) 73]] {{Hologram}} *[[Star Wars (2015) 74|''Star Wars'' (2015) 74]] *[[Star Wars (2015) 75|''Star Wars'' (2015) 75]] *{{Film|V}} {{1st}} *''[[The Empire Strikes Back: So You Want to Be a Jedi?]]'' {{Ab|The Empire Strikes Back: So You Want to Be a Jedi?
